# Evidence card — Quiet company while you work

Evidence is descriptive and preliminary. People report it helps, controlled findings are mixed or null, and no autonomous AI body double has been evaluated. No mechanism has been established.

Use only these claims, within the scope stated. None of them tested this software.

- **CLM-BD-SURVEY** (verified against the source): In one self-selected online survey of 220 adults (most identifying as neurodivergent, ADHD the most common self-identification, no diagnosis required), 186 said they were somewhat more likely or more likely to finish tasks when another person was present, and 108 said more likely. This is self-report with no comparison condition.
  Source: ["It Was Something I Naturally Found Worked and Heard About Later": An Investigation of Body Doubling with Neurodivergent Participants](https://leyabreanna.com/papers/body_double_taccess.pdf).
- **CLM-BD-VARIATION** (verified against the source): Body doubling is not one-size-fits-all: survey respondents reported it varies by person, task, mood and availability, and some found another person's presence more distracting, a source of judgement fears or guilt-driven accountability (four respondents), or hard to arrange with a partner who was not 'too chatty'; the authors note high-accountability formats can feel stressful or overwhelming.
  Source: ["It Was Something I Naturally Found Worked and Heard About Later": An Investigation of Body Doubling with Neurodivergent Participants](https://leyabreanna.com/papers/body_double_taccess.pdf).
- **CLM-BD-EEG** (checked against an abstract or summary only): A small 2025 ASSETS study (N=26; neurotypical, medicated ADHD and unmedicated ADHD participants) found no statistically significant differences between body-doubling and solo conditions on ACT reading comprehension or EEG-derived focus and calmness metrics; the authors report no consistent negative impacts and 'promising trends' for unmedicated ADHD participants.
  Source: [Reading Between the Lines: Exploring Body Doubling in ADHD Using EEG](https://doi.org/10.1145/3663547.3759743); [Evaluating the Efficacy of Body Doubling for ADHD Using a Brain-Computer Interface](https://www.ccsc.org/centralplains/2025/talks/talk-poster16/).
- **CLM-BD-VR** (verified against the source): In a non-peer-reviewed VR preprint (12 ASRS-screened adults, 20-minute bricklaying task), working with a human avatar or an 'AI' avatar both produced more bricks per minute (10.82 and 11.06) than working alone (8.49), with no difference between the two; the 'AI' double was secretly operated by a human (Wizard-of-Oz), so this does not test an autonomous AI.
  Source: [You Are Not Alone: Designing Body Doubling for ADHD in Virtual Reality](https://arxiv.org/html/2509.12153v1).
- **CLM-BD-NO-AI** (verified against the source): None of the studies reviewed here evaluated an autonomous AI body double: the VR 'AI' was human-operated (Wizard-of-Oz), the robot used random pre-programmed motions, and the roadmap reports no new data.
  Source: [You Are Not Alone: Designing Body Doubling for ADHD in Virtual Reality](https://arxiv.org/html/2509.12153v1); [A Roadmap of Mixed Reality Body Doubling for Adults with ADHD](https://arxiv.org/html/2605.07851v1); [Design and Evaluation of a Socially Assistive Robot Schoolwork Companion for College Students with ADHD](https://arxiv.org/html/2401.06289v1).
- **CLM-BD-EARLY** (verified against the source): Research on body doubling is limited and early: a 2026 work-in-progress roadmap describes it as 'a fairly new and under-researched topic', and ADHD organisations ADDA and CHADD both state that research proving its effectiveness is lacking.
  Source: [A Roadmap of Mixed Reality Body Doubling for Adults with ADHD](https://arxiv.org/html/2605.07851v1); [The ADHD Body Double: A Unique Tool for Getting Things Done](https://add.org/the-body-double/); [Could a Body Double Help You Increase Your Productivity?](https://chadd.org/adhd-weekly/could-a-body-double-help-you-increase-your-productivity/).
- **CLM-BD-MECHANISM** (verified against the source): No source reviewed here tested or established a neurochemical (for example dopamine) mechanism for body doubling. The research papers either do not mention dopamine or list other untested theories (mirror neurons, Hawthorne effect, social facilitation, accountability); consumer pages that mention dopamine or neurotransmitters present it as speculation, an inference from general social-behaviour research, or a claim attributed to a commercial service.
  Source: ["It Was Something I Naturally Found Worked and Heard About Later": An Investigation of Body Doubling with Neurodivergent Participants](https://leyabreanna.com/papers/body_double_taccess.pdf); [A Roadmap of Mixed Reality Body Doubling for Adults with ADHD](https://arxiv.org/html/2605.07851v1); [The ADHD Body Double: A Unique Tool for Getting Things Done](https://add.org/the-body-double/); [Could a Body Double Help You Increase Your Productivity?](https://chadd.org/adhd-weekly/could-a-body-double-help-you-increase-your-productivity/); [ADHD Body Doubling: What It Is and How It Works](https://www.psychcentral.com/adhd/adhd-body-doubling); [What Is 'Body Doubling' and Can It Help With ADHD?](https://health.clevelandclinic.org/body-doubling-for-adhd).
- **CLM-BD-SOCIALFAC** (checked against an abstract or summary only): In general (non-ADHD) research, a 1983 meta-analysis of 241 studies with nearly 24,000 participants found the mere presence of others had small effects: it sped up simple tasks and slowed complex ones, impaired accuracy on complex tasks and only slightly improved accuracy on simple tasks (a finding vulnerable to unpublished null results).
  Source: [Social facilitation: A meta-analysis of 241 studies](https://doi.org/10.1037/0033-2909.94.2.265).

Full register, statuses and limitations: `evidence/claims.yaml` in the source repository. Runtime snapshot: `references/shared/runtime-evidence.md`. No claim has been reviewed by a clinician.
